reasoning_steps: The normal force on the insect is N = mg cos(alpha).
The tangential component of gravity trying to pull the insect down is mg sin(alpha).
For the insect not to slip, the static friction must balance this tangential force: f = mg sin(alpha).
The maximum static friction is mu N = mu mg cos(alpha).
Therefore, mg sin(alpha) <= mu mg cos(alpha), which means tan(alpha) <= mu.
assumptions_used: Insect moves very slowly, so centripetal forces are negligible
